findings.description: Census re-derived from scratch: the clause's sweep returns 71 hits across inbox-to-memory/ and _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/, and applying the two ordered questions to every one of them leaves no surviving passage that reads as a full account of when the skill writes into _memory/ while omitting the write-through. The pre-ruled README.md:74 is fixed and now answers question 1 in its own words.
findings.evidence: Sweep: `/usr/bin/grep -rniE "sign-?off|auto-promote|automatic|per-candidate|approval|last_confirmed" inbox-to-memory/ _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/` -> 71 lines. README.md:74 now reads: "Nothing is ever promoted to memory automatically. Every record requires your explicit per-candidate approval, and unpromoted candidates keep their `[memory candidate: ...]` flag as a record of what was considered. One date is the exception. When an input restates a claim an accepted record already makes, the run stamps that input's date onto the record's `last_confirmed` and names it in the closing report, so `git status` can show modified memory files after a run where you approved nothing. No record is created and nothing a record claims is edited — only the date saying when the claim was last seen to hold."

findings.description: Both pre-ruled boundary cases came out as the clause rules them: README.md:74 changed, and the _memory.template.md "Only create record files" sentence is byte-identical to the base commit (it sits at :67 now only because the new paragraph pushed it down two lines).
findings.evidence: `git diff f027515c9f5487acd4b8d0be973af0e5bc9017d0 -- inbox-to-memory/assets/claude-md/_memory.template.md` shows exactly two added lines and zero deletions; the diff hunk header is `@@ -27,6 +27,8 @@`, entirely above the numbered procedure. Current inbox-to-memory/assets/claude-md/_memory.template.md:67 = "2. **Wait for user sign-off.** Only create record files in `_memory/` after the user reviews the groomed note and explicitly approves which candidates to crystallize." — unchanged.

findings.description: The _memory.template.md document-level obligation landed, immediately under the required-frontmatter block that lists last_confirmed at :21, and it explicitly inoculates the pre-ruled sentence below it rather than leaving the two to contradict each other.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/assets/claude-md/_memory.template.md:30 — "`last_confirmed` says when the record's claim was last seen to hold, and it is the one field here that gets written without anybody approving it. It starts as the record's own `date`. After that, when an inbox input restates a claim an `accepted` record already makes, [...stamp-confirmed.sh] stamps that input's date onto the record and never walks the date backwards. That write skips the sign-off described below and is the only one in `_memory/` that does; the run's verify report names every record it moved along with every one it declined to. Everything else here waits for the user, item by item." The key it explains is at :21; the sign-off step it forward-references is at :67.

findings.description: The machine-contracts.md obligation landed as one paragraph carrying all three lifecycle parts, and the v1 part is written as a consequence of that document's own generation table rather than as a new rule.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/references/machine-contracts.md:47 — "**`last_confirmed` is written for you, and only ever forward.** [Migration](migration.md) initializes it to the record's own `date` [...] After that, [scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh](../scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh) advances it whenever an inbox input restates a claim an `accepted` record already makes, to that input's date, with no sign-off prompt in front of the write. It refuses any candidate not later than what the record already holds. A file carrying no `schema` key gains the key by neither route, which is the first row of the table above rather than a rule of its own: v1 frontmatter sits outside this contract, so nothing here fits a v2 key onto it." The table it points back at is at :13-17, whose first row is `| no `schema` key | not checked | not checked | checked |`; nothing between :17 and :47 is a table, so the back-reference resolves. migration.md:37-39 carries the matching half, with "a review that never happened" softened to "a review the migrator has no evidence of" and a following paragraph naming the stamper.

findings.description: Questioned the category as the clause demands: two sweeps with different predicates add hits the clause's own predicate cannot reach, and the twelve-item list also omits one hit its own predicate does reach. None of the additions is a violation under the two questions, but the closest call is recorded here.
findings.evidence: Predicate B (`never (writes|modif|touch)|writes? (into|to) _memory|without asking|nothing (is|gets) written|untouched|gated|gate on|crystalliz`) adds, among others: references/scope-decisions.md:68 "**`_memory/`** is the structured layer [...] Content here is durable — once a record lands, it stays (with `status` transitions) rather than getting rewritten"; assets/readme/_memory.template.md:8; README.md:72; references/migration.md:150; assets/working-state.template.md:5,38,48. Predicate C (`stamp|confirm|last seen|stale|date onto`) adds SKILL.md:55 and retrieval-funnel.md:88-98. scope-decisions.md:68 is the closest call and still passes: question 1 answers no (the bullet already tells the reader records change in place via `status` transitions, and it makes no claim about the approval gate — its subject is content churn versus durability), and question 2 answers no (it is an account of what the layer is for, not of what the skill writes on its own). Separately, assets/claude-md/journal.template.md:23 lists `last_confirmed: YYYY-MM-DD` in the same shape as the cited `_memory.template.md:21` and is missing from the twelve even though the clause's own predicate returns it; a bare key list in a frontmatter shape block is not an account of how the value is set, the journal scope keeps entries under `entries/` rather than `_memory/`, and the clause's document-level obligation is drawn around `_memory.template.md` alone, so no edit is owed there.

findings.description: Every remaining sweep hit was judged against the two questions rather than against literal truth, and each one that survives unchanged does so because question 2 answers no — its document carries a full account elsewhere — or because the sentence is plainly about record creation, which is the shape the _memory.template.md:65 pre-ruling passes.
findings.evidence: Unchanged and passing: SKILL.md:162 ("Wait for explicit per-candidate sign-off") and SKILL.md:192 ("Every record creation requires explicit user approval per candidate") — SKILL.md now carries the Stamp Confirmations section at :140-158, the phase 6 bullets at :211-212, and the operating rule at :482, so question 2 answers no. SKILL.md:387 ("Sets `last_confirmed` on a record to the record's own date") is a bullet inside migrate mode's "What it changes" list, scoped by construction and not a lifecycle claim. references/retrieval-funnel.md:39-41 and :102 are query semantics, not write claims. assets/claude-md/client.template.md:71, project.template.md:55, assets/readme/client.template.md:34, project.template.md:37 all say "crystallized only after user sign-off" — the creation shape the :65 pre-ruling passes, and every scaffolded scope also gets `_memory/CLAUDE.md` from the template whose :30 now carries the account. _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md:35 passes on question 2 exactly as the task anticipated: T-005's scenario 5 at :120-142 now gives that document its own full account, including :126 "the stamp does not pass through that gate anyway" and the "No prompt" row at :137.

findings.description: Nothing out of bounds was edited. The working tree holds eight modified files and every one is attributable to a task's own artifact list; eval-scope.sh's change is T-006's repointing, not this task's.
findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain` -> 8 modified: EVALS.md, eval-scope.sh, README.md, SKILL.md, _memory.template.md, machine-contracts.md, migration.md, tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh (plus two untracked from T-001/T-005). `git diff <base> --stat -- tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/README.md inbox-to-memory/scripts/` prints nothing, so all of scripts/ and the "Three scopes" non-goal are untouched. SKILL.md:449's record key order is byte-identical to the suite's pin at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:616. eval-scope.sh's only hunk rewrites the `:1226` citation, which is T-006's title verbatim ("Repoint the stale smoke-suite line citation in eval-scope.sh", clause C-15, status checking). EVALS.md's four enumerations were moved by T-005 (fixture count to "Five", the fifth bullet, the Grading row, the closing line), which is that task's clause, not this one's.

findings.description: The handed-down correction to SKILL.md:152 is verified separately from C-11: the replacement claim is true against the real script, and it still gives a real reason to batch — write count and report determinism, which is the reason C-5 gives.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:152 now closes "[...] so the same inbox writes that record once or twice and reports it differently depending on which file got read first." Falsified against the shipped stamper by looping per input over one record set to 2026-01-20, notes dated 2026-02-10 and 2026-02-17. Oldest first: two `stamped:` lines (`2026-01-20 -> 2026-02-10`, then `2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17`), final `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`. Newest first: one `stamped:` line (`2026-01-20 -> 2026-02-17`) and one `skipped: ... (2026-02-10 is not later than 2026-02-17)`, final `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`. So the write count and the report differ by order while the stored record does not — the new sentence is exactly right and the old "a different record" claim is exactly what the monotonic guard falsifies.
